1.summary: Jude urges believers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints, because ungodly intruders pervert grace; he recalls judgments on Israel in the wilderness, rebellious angels and Sodom, describes the intruders with vivid images, and calls the faithful to build themselves up, pray, wait for mercy, and rescue others, ending with a great doxology.
1.lookfor: Notice the groups of three throughout, and the doxology that closes the letter.

names.name: Jude
names.gloss: A brother of James and of Jesus.

names.name: James
names.gloss: Jesus' brother, leader of the Jerusalem church.

names.name: Michael
names.gloss: The archangel, protector of God's people.

names.name: Cain
names.gloss: Adam's son, who murdered his brother.

names.name: Balaam
names.gloss: A prophet who led Israel astray for profit.

names.name: Korah
names.gloss: A Levite who rebelled against Moses and was swallowed by the earth.

names.name: Enoch
names.gloss: The seventh from Adam, who walked with God.

insights.title: Servant and brother
insights.body: Jude calls himself servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James (1:1). Like James, he once doubted his brother; now he calls him Lord.

insights.title: Contend
insights.body: Contend earnestly for the faith once for all delivered to the saints (1:3). The verb is an athlete's word for straining in a contest. The faith is a fixed deposit, handed down, not reinvented.

insights.title: Three warnings
insights.body: Jude recalls Israel saved from Egypt yet destroyed for unbelief, angels who left their place, and Sodom and Gomorrah (1:5-7). Privilege didn't protect them.

insights.title: Michael and Moses' body
insights.body: When Michael disputed with the devil over Moses' body, he didn't dare bring a slanderous judgment but said, the Lord rebuke you (1:9). The story isn't in the Old Testament; it comes from a Jewish writing, probably the Assumption of Moses.

insights.title: Enoch's prophecy
insights.body: Enoch prophesied, the Lord comes with ten thousands of his holy ones (1:14-15). Jude quotes 1 Enoch, a Jewish book well known in his day, which isn't in the Old Testament; he uses it as a recognized voice.

insights.title: Clouds without water
insights.body: They are hidden rocks in your love feasts, clouds without water, autumn trees without fruit, wild waves foaming out their shame, wandering stars (1:12-13). Every image is of something that promises and fails.

insights.title: Keep yourselves
insights.body: Build yourselves up in faith, pray in the Holy Spirit, keep yourselves in God's love, wait for mercy (1:20-21). And have mercy on those who doubt; snatch others out of the fire (1:22-23).

insights.title: Able to keep you
insights.body: To him who is able to keep you from stumbling and present you blameless before his glory with great joy (1:24). After all the warnings, the letter ends with God's power to keep his people. Believers keep themselves (1:21) because God keeps them.

insights.title: Mercy for doubters
insights.body: Jude asks believers to have mercy on those who doubt. Who do you know who is struggling with faith, and how could you show them mercy?

intro.who: Jude, servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James (1:1), traditionally Judas, one of Jesus' brothers. Like James, he doesn't claim to be the Lord's brother, only his servant.
intro.when: Uncertain; perhaps AD 60–80. 2 Peter 2 shares much of its material.
intro.why: Jude meant to write about their shared salvation but had to urge readers instead to contend for the faith, because ungodly people had crept in, turning God's grace into license and rejecting authority. He reminds them of past judgments and calls them to keep themselves in God's love.

outline.title: Contend for the faith; kept by God
